findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The elsif branch of website_name (sibling-subdomain case, advertised by its own comment "www.example.com == forum.example.com") is the only new branch exercised by zero tests in this diff. Tracing the three added specs in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb (lines 75-90): the discourse.org test takes the else branch (2-label hosts fail the length>2 guard), the example.com test takes the if branch, and the forums.example.com test takes the else branch (2 vs 3 labels fail the equal-length guard) — the elsif's split/join comparison at user_serializer.rb:146 is never executed by any spec the diff adds, so a regression in the label-slicing comparison (e.g. changing [1..-1] or the > 2 guard) silently breaks full-path display for www-style websites on multi-label instances and the entire suite still passes; the behavior this diff's own line 145 comment claims to deliver ships unvalidated.

[BUG] Ruby's strict URI parser raises URI::InvalidURIError for stored website strings containing non-ASCII IDN hosts (e.g. http://例え.jp/profile) or spaces in the path (e.g. http://example.com/my page), so the rescue returns nil, website_name becomes nil while include_website_name still returns true (website is present), and the {{#if model.website_name}} guard in user.hbs hides the website row that the removed client-side website.split("/")[2] computation displayed. Users whose saved website URL contains any character Ruby's URI parser rejects lose the website link from their profile entirely after this change — the globe icon and anchor disappear even though model.website is still set and the old code rendered a host label for exactly these values.

[ADVISORY] The elsif branch (equal-label-count sibling domains, the author's documented 'www.example.com == forum.example.com' case) has zero spec coverage: all three added specs in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb use the two-label website example.com, and the elsif guard requires both hosts to have more than 2 labels, so the [1..-1] suffix comparison at line 147 never executes under the suite. An inversion or off-by-one in the most convoluted line of the new logic ships undetected — every instance hosted on a subdomain (forum.example.com) renders www-prefixed user websites wrong and no spec fails, even though this branch is one of the three behaviors the PR claims to implement.

[ADVISORY] The new exclusion gate include_website_name and the nil-host return path have no spec: the only added test context ('with filled out website') always sets a website, so the suite never asserts that the website_name key is absent for users without a website or with an unparseable one. A regression in the exclusion path — e.g. the method missing the serializer framework's include_#{attr}? predicate suffix, which turns the gate into a silent no-op emitting website_name: null on every user payload — ships undetected, because no example in this diff covers the website-absent population that the gate exists to protect.

[BUG] The display string is built from URI(...).host plus URI(...).path only, discarding the port and the query string: http://example.com:3000/admin?tab=2 renders as example.com/admin on same-domain instances and bare example.com elsewhere, whereas the removed client-side split("/")[2] display preserved the port (example.com:3000). Profiles linking self-hosted services on nonstandard ports — common among self-hosted Discourse communities — display a label that implies port 80 instead of the real destination, and two links differing only by query string render identically; because website_host + URI(website.to_s).path is duplicated in all three branches (lines 144, 147, 150), fixing it takes three coordinated edits.

[ADVISORY] The same-domain heuristic is asymmetric: a website that is a subdomain of the instance domain (www.example.com/user on instance example.com) falls to the else branch, fails discourse_host.ends_with?('.www.example.com'), and shows host-only — while the mirror case (website example.com on instance forums.example.com) and the equal-length sibling case both show the full path. Operators running on apex domains (example.com) get the requirement 'show complete path when domains match' satisfied in only one direction: users' www-prefixed links to the very same site render truncated on the profile, while the reverse instance configuration renders them expanded.

[ADVISORY] The complete-path display is wired only into the profile page template; the user-card surface that renders the same website field through its own duplicate client-side host extraction (websiteName computed from website.split("/")[2] in the user-card controller) is untouched, leaving two divergent implementations of the same display rule. The same user's website renders bare-host on the user card but host-plus-path on the profile, and any future fix to the display rule must be applied in two places — the serializer spec suite added in this diff cannot see the card copy at all.

[BUG] The same-domain matching in website_name is directional: a website host with more labels than the instance host (www.example.com/t/topic/1 when the instance is example.com) fails every branch — the elsif requires equal label counts and the else requires discourse_host to end with ".#{website_host}" — and renders host-only text, even though the elsif itself declares sibling subdomains of the same registrable domain equivalent. A forum hosted at an apex domain (example.com) displays plain "www.example.com" (or "docs.example.com") for links into its own www/subdomain mirror, so the feature this PR exists for silently fails for that entire deployment class, while the mirror-image case (instance www.example.com, website example.com/...) shows the full path — a transitivity break in the code's own equivalence policy; none of the three new specs exercises a website host with more labels than the instance host, so CI cannot catch the gap.

[BUG] include_website_name lacks the trailing ? that the ActiveModel::Serializers include_#{attribute}? conditional-inclusion hook dispatches, so the guard is never invoked and website_name is serialized for every user. Every UserSerializer payload for a user without a website now carries website_name: null (profiles, cards, admin views), the author's include-only-when-website-present intent silently fails, and because the diff adds no website-absent spec the dead guard ships undetected — a maintainer reading the serializer will believe the attribute is conditionally included when it never is.

[ADVISORY] The three new serializer specs cover only host==instance, host==parent-of-instance, and unrelated-host, leaving both outcomes of the elsif branch (user_serializer.rb:144-146, sibling-subdomain matching) completely untested. Any refactor of the sibling comparison — its label-count gate or the [1..-1] join — passes the full suite, so the display behavior for sibling subdomains, the one branch whose policy the requirement text never sanctions, can regress or be deleted with zero test signal.

[BUG] The sibling-equivalence check approximates "same registrable domain" by comparing label counts and joining labels after the first, which has no public-suffix awareness and therefore classifies unrelated tenants under shared registrable domains as the same site. An instance at forum.herokuapp.com (or user.github.io, or foo.co.uk) treats any sibling tenant's URL as same-domain and displays its full path — other.herokuapp.com/their/page renders as "other.herokuapp.com/their/page" instead of the previous host-only text — displaying paths of sites unrelated to the instance, an expansion the stated requirement ("website domain is same as instance domain") never asked for.

[ADVISORY] The profile template now gates the website row on the new server-computed model.website_name with no fallback to model.website, hard-coupling display to a field the deleted client-side computed property (which derived the host from model.website alone) did not need. Any payload that includes website but not website_name — an old app server behind the load balancer during a rolling multi-web deploy, or a future serializer path serving this template without the new attribute — renders no website at all on the profile instead of degrading to the old host-only display.

[ADVISORY] website_name parses URI(website.to_s) at four separate expression sites (the initial host read plus three .path reads) with an inline modifier rescue, re-parsing the same string up to twice per call. A future edit to one of the three URI(website.to_s).path expressions (for example adding query-string display after one branch only) drifts the branches apart silently, and the modifier rescue on line 138 swallows every StandardError from the first parse; parsing once into a local with a single nil-guard deletes the three duplicate parse expressions and confines the rescue to one place.

[BUG] `website_name` builds the displayed text by concatenating `URI(website.to_s).host` with the raw `URI(website.to_s).path`, and `URI#path` returns "/" for scheme-only URLs while excluding query string, fragment, and port, so same-domain websites display as `example.com/` and query- or port-distinguished URLs lose the distinguishing part of the URL. A user on instance example.com whose website is exactly `http://example.com` now shows 'example.com/' where the removed client-side `website.split("/")[2]` displayed 'example.com'; `http://example.com/page?id=3` displays as 'example.com/page' and a same-domain URL on `:3000` shows no port, so the profile's displayed link text no longer identifies the actual target the href points to.

[BUG] The same-domain comparison is case-sensitive (`website_host == discourse_host`, `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`) while DNS hostnames are case-insensitive and Ruby's `URI#host` preserves the stored case of the website URL, so a stored `http://Example.com/user` never matches a lowercase `Discourse.current_hostname` of `example.com`. Users whose saved website URL contains mixed-case host letters get only the bare host displayed on the very instance whose domain matches — the full-path feature the PR exists to deliver silently no-ops for exactly the inputs it was written for, and no error surfaces because the elsif/else fall back to host-only display.

[BUG] `website_name` returns nil for any stored website that Ruby's `URI()` raises on (`rescue nil`, e.g. a URL with an internal space like `http://foo bar.com` or unencoded non-ASCII), and the template now gates the entire website row on `{{#if model.website_name}}` (user.hbs line 66), whereas the removed client-side `website.split("/")[2]` displayed the host for those same values. After this deploy, users whose previously-rendered malformed website URLs survive in the database lose the globe icon and website link from their profile entirely, with no error anywhere — `model.website` is still serialized and present but nothing renders it.

[ADVISORY] The sibling-subdomain branch — the elsif comparing `website_host.split('.')[1..-1]` suffixes behind the `discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` guard, i.e. the `www.example.com == forum.example.com` case the code comment names — is exercised by none of the three new specs, which all hit the equality branch or the parent-suffix branch. The next editor of this heuristic (or a regression in the `[1..-1]` slicing, the `> 2` guard, or the ternary) ships green because the most intricate branch of the new logic has zero coverage, and sibling-domain users silently stop getting — or wrongly get — full-path display.

[BUG] The label-suffix heuristic treats any two hosts sharing two or more trailing labels as the same domain, so for instances addressed by a raw IP a website on a different IP that shares the trailing octets passes the sibling comparison (website `http://9.0.0.9/page` on instance `10.0.0.9` compares `[1..-1]` as '0.0.9' == '0.0.9'). Intranet/internal Discourse instances bound to an IP address display a foreign machine's full path as though it were the same site — the registrable-domain semantics of the parent/sibling rule are meaningless for numeric hosts, and nothing in the guards excludes them.

[BUG] `include_website_name` is defined without the `?` suffix required by the serializer framework's conditional-attribute hook (`include_#{attribute}?`, the convention used by `include_name?`/`include_email?` throughout this codebase and by the include methods that `untrusted_attributes` generates), so this method is never invoked and the `website.present?` gate it was written for is inert dead code. `website_name` is emitted under whatever gate `untrusted_attributes` registers instead of the author's presence check, so every user payload for a user with no website carries `"website_name": null` — the presence constraint this diff introduces silently fails to hold, and no spec covers the no-website case that would have caught the broken hook.

[BUG] The elsif classifies any two hosts with equal label counts greater than 2 as 'same domain' whenever all labels after the first are equal, so on an instance hosted directly under a two-label public suffix (forum.co.uk, forums.com.au, bbs.co.jp) every user website under that same suffix (shop.co.uk, news.com.au) is wrongly matched. On instances hosted under multi-label public suffixes, unrelated external sites receive the full-path treatment the PR reserved for the instance's own domain — a profile displays 'shop.co.uk/deals' as if it were an internal link — a silent widening of the accepted objective 'website domain is same as instance domain' to 'shares a two-label suffix'; the new specs never exercise it because every fixture uses example.com-style two-label TLDs.

[ADVISORY] The website row is gated on the server-derived key `model.website_name` instead of the underlying datum `model.website`, discarding the old design in which the label was computed client-side from `website` and therefore could never be missing while `website` was present. Any payload that includes `website` but lacks `website_name` — an old web host behind the load balancer during a rolling deploy serving a browser that loaded the new JS bundle, or any future serializer that reuses this template's model — hides the user's website row entirely instead of degrading to the host-only label; visitors see the element vanish with no fallback because a derived value was promoted to the presence signal for the primary datum.

[ADVISORY] For same-domain websites that are the bare root with a trailing slash (http://example.com/), `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` appends the root path '/' and the displayed label renders as 'example.com/'. A user whose website is exactly the instance root URL gets 'example.com/' shown on their profile — the one same-domain shape (empty path) the new specs do not cover — which reads as a typo and was never part of the accepted 'show complete URL path' intent.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten profile-website anchor keeps target="_blank" with no rel="noopener noreferrer" while binding href to the user-controlled model.website, so the opened page retains a live window.opener handle to the Discourse tab. Any user can set their profile website to a page they control; when a viewer clicks the globe link, the opened page can call window.opener.location to redirect the victim's still-open Discourse tab to a phishing clone of the instance (reverse tabnabbing) — this diff re-emits exactly this anchor markup for the user-supplied URL and leaves the opener protection absent.

[ADVISORY] None of the three tests added in this diff can execute the new elsif branch of UserSerializer#website_name (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:145-147): every added test uses website host 'example.com' (two labels), so the predicate (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2 evaluates false in all three cases ('discourse.org' 2v2 fails >2, 'example.com' 2v2 fails >2 and never reaches it, 'forums.example.com' 3v2 fails equality). The sibling-domain case the branch exists for — 'www.example.com' on a 'forum.example.com' instance, per the branch's own comment — and both of its inner ternary outcomes ship with zero executed assertions; a wrong [1..-1] slice index or an inverted ternary passes CI and breaks path display for users of every instance whose hostname has 3+ labels (e.g. meta.discourse.org). Test files checked: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb is the only test file in this diff and its three added tests are the complete set of website_name assertions.

[BUG] The elsif branch compares registrable domains by dropping only the first label (split('.')[1..-1]), so two unrelated registrations under the same multi-label public suffix compare equal. On an instance hosted at e.g. blog.com.br, a user's website 'http://loja.com.br/products' is classified as same-site and the profile displays the full 'loja.com.br/products' instead of the host alone; because no test in this diff executes this branch at all, the misclassification ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] The equal-host test asserts only the pathed URL ('http://example.com/user'); the diff replaced the context's original bare fixture 'http://example.com' with a pathed one and never pins what website_name returns for a same-domain website with no path, where website_host + URI(website.to_s).path concatenates the empty string. The dominant real-world stored-website shape (bare 'http://example.com') has its display-name result unpinned — a refactor of the concatenation that yields 'example.com/' instead of 'example.com' mangles every same-site profile name while CI stays green.

[ADVISORY] The else branch detects same-site only in the parent direction (discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)), so 'http://www.example.com/page' on an instance hosted at 'example.com' returns host-only, while the semantically identical sibling case ('www.example.com' on 'forum.example.com') returns the full path. Admins of apex-hosted instances (hostname 'example.com') see the feature silently not apply to their own www-prefixed profile websites; no test pins this asymmetry and nothing in the diff documents it as intended, so it reads as an oversight of the 'same as instance domain' contract in the PR title.

[BUG] The elsif branch matches any two hosts whose labels after the first are identical, so on an instance whose hostname is a registrable domain under a multi-label public suffix (Discourse.current_hostname = 'example.co.uk'), a website on a completely different registrable domain ('http://other.co.uk/some-page') is treated as the instance's own domain and serialized with its full path. Users on .co.uk/.com.au/.org.uk-style instances see the complete URL path rendered as the website name for sites that are not the instance's domain (e.g. 'other.co.uk/some-page' instead of 'other.co.uk'), violating the feature's stated rule (show the full path only when the website domain is the instance domain) and misleading profile viewers; the href stays correct so nothing crashes or links wrong.

[ADVISORY] The three website_name specs cover only exact-host match, parent-domain match, and different-domain, leaving the elsif subdomain-variant branch (serializer lines 144-146, the 'www.example.com == forum.example.com' case) completely untested. A regression or false positive in the subdomain-matching branch ships undetected by CI; the public-suffix false positive living in exactly that branch ('other.co.uk' vs 'example.co.uk' matching on their shared 'co.uk' tail) is precisely the class of bug these added specs cannot catch.

[ADVISORY] website_name calls URI(website.to_s) up to three times per serialization (lines 138, 143, 146, 149) with the inline `rescue nil` guarding only the first parse, making the method's crash-safety depend on the positional fact that later calls repeat an already-succeeded pure parse; hoisting `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil` plus an early return deletes the redundant parses and the guard asymmetry. Every user-page serialization performs three URI parses, and the next maintainer who extends this method (e.g. adding a .query display) or hoists the parse without carrying the rescue turns any malformed website string — the profile website column is unvalidated free text — into an uncaught URI::InvalidURIError, 500ing every payload that serializes that user.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than an observed functional defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves `websiteName` from a permissive client-side `website.split("/")[2]` to a server-side `website_name` derived via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` (user_serializer.rb). If `URI(...)` raises (e.g., due to spaces or non-ASCII hosts), `website_host` becomes nil and `website_name` returns nil, while `include_website_name` still returns true whenever `website.present?`. The template was changed to `{{#if model.website_name}} ... {{/if}}`, so a nil `website_name` hides the entire website display even though `model.website` is still set, causing a regression for stored website strings that Ruby’s URI parser rejects.

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` has an `elsif` branch guarded by `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` **and** `discourse_host.split('.').length > 2`, intended for sibling subdomains (comment: `# www.example.com == forum.example.com`). In the added specs, `user.user_profile.website` is always `http://example.com/user` (2 labels), while `Discourse.current_hostname` is stubbed to `discourse.org` (2), `example.com` (2), and `forums.example.com` (3). None of these combinations satisfy the `elsif` guard (either label count is 2, or counts differ 2 vs 3), so the `[1..-1]` suffix-compare line in that branch is never executed by the suite. This is a concrete missing coverage gap for nontrivial logic, not a proven functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `website_name` plus an inclusion gate method `include_website_name` in `user_serializer.rb`, but the only new specs are under `context "with filled out website"` where `user.user_profile.website` is always set. There is no coverage asserting that `website_name` is omitted when `website` is blank, nor that an unparseable URL (where `URI(...).host` becomes nil and `website_name` returns nil) behaves as intended. The note about a potential misnamed include predicate (missing `?`) is speculative from this diff alone, but the lack of tests for the exclusion/nil-host paths is directly evidenced.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the display label is constructed from `URI(website.to_s).host` and sometimes `+ URI(...).path` (duplicated across branches). `URI#host` omits the port, and the code never appends `URI#query`/`#fragment`, so inputs like `http://example.com:3000/admin?tab=2` will render as `example.com/admin` (or `example.com`), losing `:3000` and the query. This is a concrete behavior change from the removed client-side `split("/")[2]`, which would have included `example.com:3000` in the label.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “same site”/parent-domain logic is one-directional. For an apex instance (`discourse_host = "example.com"`) and a user website on a subdomain (`website_host = "www.example.com"`), it falls into the final `else` and checks `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` (i.e., `"example.com".ends_with?(".www.example.com")`), which is false, so it returns only `website_host` and drops the path. The reverse case (instance `forums.example.com`, website `example.com/user`) *does* include the path via `ends_with?(".example.com")`. This asymmetry is directly implied by the diff and causes inconsistent/truncated display for common `www.` links.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The complete-path display is wired only into the profile page template; the user-card surface that renders the same website field through its own duplicate client-side host extraction (websiteName computed from website.split("/")[2] in the user-card controller) is untouched, leaving two divergent implementations of the same display rule. adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows changes to the user profile controller/template and the user serializer/spec. It removes `websiteName` from `controllers/user.js.es6` and updates `templates/user/user.hbs` to use `model.website_name`, but it contains no user-card controller/template code. The finding’s claim about an untouched “user-card controller” still using `website.split("/")[2]` and causing divergent behavior cannot be verified from this diff alone.

A forum hosted at an apex domain (example.com) displays plain "www.example.com" (or "docs.example.com") for links into its own www/subdomain mirror, so the feature this PR exists for silently fails for that entire deployment class, while the mirror-image case (instance www.example.com, website example.com/...) shows the full path — a transitivity break in the code's own equivalence policy; none of the three new specs exercises a website host with more labels than the instance host, so CI cannot catch the gap.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, when `discourse_host` is an apex domain like `example.com` and `website_host` is a subdomain like `www.example.com`, none of the branches append the path: `website_host == discourse_host` is false, the `elsif` requires equal label counts (3 vs 2), and the `else` only appends the path when `discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)` (i.e., when the instance is a subdomain of the website host), which is the opposite direction. The result is returning just `website_host` (e.g., `www.example.com`) instead of `www.example.com/user`, creating inconsistent behavior relative to the sibling-subdomain equivalence logic. The added specs do not cover this case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] include_website_name lacks the trailing ? that the ActiveModel::Serializers include_#{attribute}? conditional-inclusion hook dispatches, so the guard is never invoked and website_name is serialized for every user. Every UserSerializer payload for a user without a website now carries website_name: null (profiles, cards, admin views), the author's include-only-when-website-present intent silently fails, and because the diff adds no website-absent spec the dead guard ships undetected — a maintainer reading the serializer will believe the attribute is conditionally included when it never is.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` the PR adds `def website_name` plus a guard `def include_website_name` (no `?`). In ActiveModel::Serializers the conditional inclusion hook is conventionally `include_<attr>?`; if that convention is in effect here, this method will never be called and `website_name` will be serialized unconditionally (nil for users without a website), contradicting the apparent intent of `website.present?`. The diff also adds no spec for the website-absent case, so this would ship undetected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The three new serializer specs cover only host==instance, host==parent-of-instance, and unrelated-host, leaving both outcomes of the elsif branch (user_serializer.rb:144-146, sibling-subdomain matching) completely untested. Any refactor of the sibling comparison — its label-count gate or the [1..-1] join — passes the full suite, so the display behavior for sibling subdomains, the one branch whose policy the requirement text never sanctions, can regress or be deleted with zero test signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including an `elsif` for “sibling subdomain” cases: `(website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` with a `[1..-1].join('.')` comparison (user_serializer.rb ~144-146). The added specs cover `host == instance` (first `if`), `website domain is parent of instance domain` (the final `else` using `ends_with?`), and `unrelated-host` (also final `else`). There is no spec that exercises either outcome of the `elsif` branch (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` matching vs non-matching), so that branch’s behavior could change or regress without test signal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sibling-equivalence check approximates "same registrable domain" by comparing label counts and joining labels after the first, which has no public-suffix awareness and therefore classifies unrelated tenants under shared registrable domains as the same site. An instance at forum.herokuapp.com (or user.github.io, or foo.co.uk) treats any sibling tenant's URL as same-domain and displays its full path — other.herokuapp.com/their/page renders as "other.herokuapp.com/their/page" instead of the previous host-only text — displaying paths of sites unrelated to the instance, an expansion the stated requirement ("website domain is same as instance domain") never asked for.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the branch `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` treats hosts as “same site” when all labels except the first match, and then returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. This will consider `forum.herokuapp.com` and `other.herokuapp.com` equivalent (both 3 labels; suffix `herokuapp.com` matches), causing the serializer to include the full path for unrelated sibling tenants. The diff shows no public-suffix/registrable-domain awareness, so the misclassification described is a real, diff-grounded correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The profile template now gates the website row on the new server-computed model.website_name with no fallback to model.website, hard-coupling display to a field the deleted client-side computed property (which derived the host from model.website alone) did not need. Any payload that includes website but not website_name — an old app server behind the load balancer during a rolling multi-web deploy, or a future serializer path serving this template without the new attribute — renders no website at all on the profile instead of degrading to the old host-only display.

adjudication.rationale: The template change replaces `{{#if websiteName}} ... {{websiteName}}` with `{{#if model.website_name}} ... {{model.website_name}}` (user.hbs), and the client-side computed `websiteName` derived from `model.website` was removed (controller). While this PR also adds `website_name` to the serializer with `include_website_name` when `website.present?`, there is no fallback in the template to show anything based on `model.website` alone. That creates a tighter coupling to the new serialized field; the reviewer’s rolling-deploy/older-payload scenario is plausible, though not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] website_name parses URI(website.to_s) at four separate expression sites (the initial host read plus three .path reads) with an inline modifier rescue, re-parsing the same string up to twice per call. A future edit to one of the three URI(website.to_s).path expressions (for example adding query-string display after one branch only) drifts the branches apart silently, and the modifier rescue on line 138 swallows every StandardError from the first parse; parsing once into a local with a single nil-guard deletes the three duplicate parse expressions and confines the rescue to one place.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the diff shows `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and then repeats `URI(website.to_s).path` in multiple branches (`website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`). This necessarily reparses the same string (host parse + one path parse) and creates duplicated parse expressions across branches, which is a concrete maintainability concern. The inline `rescue nil` also swallows any StandardError from the initial parse, and parsing once into a local URI object with a single nil-guard would remove the duplication and confine error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `website_name` builds the displayed text by concatenating `URI(website.to_s).host` with the raw `URI(website.to_s).path`, and `URI#path` returns "/" for scheme-only URLs while excluding query string, fragment, and port, so same-domain websites display as `example.com/` and query- or port-distinguished URLs lose the distinguishing part of the URL. A user on instance example.com whose website is exactly `http://example.com` now shows 'example.com/' where the removed client-side `website.split("/")[2]` displayed 'example.com'; `http://example.com/page?id=3` displays as 'example.com/page' and a same-domain URL on `:3000` shows no port, so the profile's displayed link text no longer identifies the actual target the href points to.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the displayed text is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in several same-domain/related-domain branches. `URI#path` will be `"/"` for a URL like `http://example.com`, producing `"example.com/"` (different from the removed client-side `website.split("/")[2]` which showed `"example.com"`). Also, because it uses `host` (not `host:port`) and only appends `path` (excluding query/fragment), the displayed `website_name` can omit distinguishing parts of the actual `href` (`model.website`), e.g., `?id=3` or `:3000` are not represented. This mismatch is directly implied by the diff’s Ruby code and the template switching to `model.website_name`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The same-domain comparison is case-sensitive (`website_host == discourse_host`, `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`) while DNS hostnames are case-insensitive and Ruby's `URI#host` preserves the stored case of the website URL, so a stored `http://Example.com/user` never matches a lowercase `Discourse.current_hostname` of `example.com`. Users whose saved website URL contains mixed-case host letters get only the bare host displayed on the very instance whose domain matches — the full-path feature the PR exists to deliver silently no-ops for exactly the inputs it was written for, and no error surfaces because the elsif/else fall back to host-only display.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, all hostname comparisons are done with case-sensitive string operators (`website_host == discourse_host`, `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`), and the diff shows no explicit normalization (e.g., `downcase`) of either value. That makes mixed-case host input a potential edge case where same-domain/parent-domain detection could fail, depending on what `URI(...).host` and `Discourse.current_hostname` return at runtime. The finding’s claimed behavior hinges on Ruby URI host-casing details not shown in the diff, so it’s not fully verifiable as an actual bug from the PR alone, but it is a concrete robustness issue in the newly added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `website_name` returns nil for any stored website that Ruby's `URI()` raises on (`rescue nil`, e.g. a URL with an internal space like `http://foo bar.com` or unencoded non-ASCII), and the template now gates the entire website row on `{{#if model.website_name}}` (user.hbs line 66), whereas the removed client-side `website.split("/")[2]` displayed the host for those same values. After this deploy, users whose previously-rendered malformed website URLs survive in the database lose the globe icon and website link from their profile entirely, with no error anywhere — `model.website` is still serialized and present but nothing renders it.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` is computed via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`, so any website value that causes `URI()` to raise will yield `nil`. The template was changed to gate rendering on `{{#if model.website_name}}` and display `{{model.website_name}}` (user.hbs), whereas the removed client-side `websiteName` used a simple `split("/")[2]` and would still return a host-ish string for some malformed URLs. As a result, profiles with previously stored but URI-invalid `website` values can still serialize `website` but will render no globe/link because `website_name` is nil and the `#if` prevents display.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sibling-subdomain branch — the elsif comparing `website_host.split('.')[1..-1]` suffixes behind the `discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` guard, i.e. the `www.example.com == forum.example.com` case the code comment names — is exercised by none of the three new specs, which all hit the equality branch or the parent-suffix branch. The next editor of this heuristic (or a regression in the `[1..-1]` slicing, the `> 2` guard, or the ternary) ships green because the most intricate branch of the new logic has zero coverage, and sibling-domain users silently stop getting — or wrongly get — full-path display.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` with three cases: (1) `website_host == discourse_host`, (2) the sibling-subdomain `elsif` guarded by `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && ... > 2`, and (3) the parent-suffix `else` using `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`. The three new specs exercise only (1) equality (`current_hostname == 'example.com'`) and (3) the parent-suffix case (`current_hostname == 'forums.example.com'` with `website_host == 'example.com'`), plus a non-match else case (`discourse.org`). None set both hosts to the same number of dot parts > 2 (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), so the sibling-subdomain branch is untested as the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The label-suffix heuristic treats any two hosts sharing two or more trailing labels as the same domain, so for instances addressed by a raw IP a website on a different IP that shares the trailing octets passes the sibling comparison (website `http://9.0.0.9/page` on instance `10.0.0.9` compares `[1..-1]` as '0.0.9' == '0.0.9'). Intranet/internal Discourse instances bound to an IP address display a foreign machine's full path as though it were the same site — the registrable-domain semantics of the parent/sibling rule are meaningless for numeric hosts, and nothing in the guards excludes them.

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` uses a “sibling subdomain” heuristic: when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and length > 2, it compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1]` to `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]` and, if equal, returns `website_host + URI(...).path`. For numeric IP hosts this misbehaves: e.g. instance `10.0.0.9` vs website `9.0.0.9` both have 4 labels and `[1..-1]` equals `0.0.9`, so it incorrectly treats them as related and returns the full path (`9.0.0.9/page`). The diff contains no guard excluding IPs, so the finding is a real defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `include_website_name` is defined without the `?` suffix required by the serializer framework's conditional-attribute hook (`include_#{attribute}?`, the convention used by `include_name?`/`include_email?` throughout this codebase and by the include methods that `untrusted_attributes` generates), so this method is never invoked and the `website.present?` gate it was written for is inert dead code. `website_name` is emitted under whatever gate `untrusted_attributes` registers instead of the author's presence check, so every user payload for a user with no website carries `"website_name": null` — the presence constraint this diff introduces silently fails to hold, and no spec covers the no-website case that would have caught the broken hook.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` the diff adds `def include_website_name` (no trailing `?`) intended to conditionally include the new `website_name` attribute only when `website.present?`. In Discourse serializers, conditional attribute hooks are conventionally `include_<attr>?`; as written, this method will not be used as the include-hook for `website_name`, so the intended presence gate is ineffective. Since `:website_name` is added to `untrusted_attributes`, the attribute will still be serialized under whatever default include behavior `untrusted_attributes` provides, which can result in `website_name: null` when no website is set. The added specs only cover the “with filled out website” context and do not exercise the no-website case that would reveal this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The elsif classifies any two hosts with equal label counts greater than 2 as 'same domain' whenever all labels after the first are equal, so on an instance hosted directly under a two-label public suffix (forum.co.uk, forums.com.au, bbs.co.jp) every user website under that same suffix (shop.co.uk, news.com.au) is wrongly matched. On instances hosted under multi-label public suffixes, unrelated external sites receive the full-path treatment the PR reserved for the instance's own domain — a profile displays 'shop.co.uk/deals' as if it were an internal link — a silent widening of the accepted objective 'website domain is same as instance domain' to 'shares a two-label suffix'; the new specs never exercise it because every fixture uses example.com-style two-label TLDs.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the `elsif` branch triggers when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and that length is `> 2`, then treats the domains as related if all labels after the first match (`website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`). For hosts like `forum.co.uk` vs `shop.co.uk` (or `forums.com.au` vs `news.com.au`), this comparison reduces to matching `co.uk` / `com.au`, which will be true for unrelated sites under the same public suffix, causing the code to return `website_host + URI(website).path` (full-path treatment) incorrectly. The added specs only use `example.com`-style hosts (2 labels) and therefore never exercise this faulty branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The website row is gated on the server-derived key `model.website_name` instead of the underlying datum `model.website`, discarding the old design in which the label was computed client-side from `website` and therefore could never be missing while `website` was present. Any payload that includes `website` but lacks `website_name` — an old web host behind the load balancer during a rolling deploy serving a browser that loaded the new JS bundle, or any future serializer that reuses this template's model — hides the user's website row entirely instead of degrading to the host-only label; visitors see the element vanish with no fallback because a derived value was promoted to the presence signal for the primary datum.

adjudication.rationale: The template now gates display on `{{#if model.website_name}}` (user.hbs) after removing the client-side `websiteName` computed property (controller). In this diff, the serializer does add `website_name` and `include_website_name` when `website.present?`, so under a fully-updated server it will be present. However, the new JS bundle has no fallback to `model.website` if `website_name` is absent/nil, so any response that includes `website` but not `website_name` (e.g., older server version during rollout or other serializer/model reuse) would hide the website row entirely. This is a concrete compatibility/robustness concern introduced by switching the presence check to a derived field.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] For same-domain websites that are the bare root with a trailing slash (http://example.com/), `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` appends the root path '/' and the displayed label renders as 'example.com/'. A user whose website is exactly the instance root URL gets 'example.com/' shown on their profile — the one same-domain shape (empty path) the new specs do not cover — which reads as a typo and was never part of the accepted 'show complete URL path' intent.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the same-domain branch returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. For a root URL like `http://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` is `'/'`, so the label becomes `'example.com/'`. The template now displays `{{model.website_name}}`, whereas the removed client-side `websiteName` previously displayed only the host (`split("/")[2]`), so this diff introduces a visible trailing-slash regression for the instance root URL. The added specs cover `/user` but not the root-path case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten profile-website anchor keeps target="_blank" with no rel="noopener noreferrer" while binding href to the user-controlled model.website, so the opened page retains a live window.opener handle to the Discourse tab. Any user can set their profile website to a page they control; when a viewer clicks the globe link, the opened page can call window.opener.location to redirect the victim's still-open Discourse tab to a phishing clone of the instance (reverse tabnabbing) — this diff re-emits exactly this anchor markup for the user-supplied URL and leaves the opener protection absent.

adjudication.rationale: In `user/user.hbs`, the website link still renders `target="_blank"` while `rel` is only conditionally set to `'nofollow'` (`rel={{unless removeNoFollow 'nofollow'}}`), never adding `noopener`/`noreferrer`. The `href` remains bound to the user-controlled `model.website`. This leaves `window.opener` available to the opened page (reverse tabnabbing risk). The diff touches and re-emits this exact anchor markup without adding opener protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] None of the three tests added in this diff can execute the new elsif branch of UserSerializer#website_name (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:145-147): every added test uses website host 'example.com' (two labels), so the predicate (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2 evaluates false in all three cases ('discourse.org' 2v2 fails >2, 'example.com' 2v2 fails >2 and never reaches it, 'forums.example.com' 3v2 fails equality). The sibling-domain case the branch exists for — 'www.example.com' on a 'forum.example.com' instance, per the branch's own comment — and both of its inner ternary outcomes ship with zero executed assertions; a wrong [1..-1] slice index or an inverted ternary passes CI and breaks path display for users of every instance whose hostname has 3+ labels (e.g. meta.discourse.org). Test files checked: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb is the only test file in this diff and its three added tests are the complete set of website_name assertions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` (including an `elsif` intended for sibling subdomains like `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), but the new specs only use `website_host = example.com` (2 labels). As a result, none of the added tests can make `(website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` true, so the new `elsif` branch (and both outcomes of its inner ternary) is untested. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The elsif branch compares registrable domains by dropping only the first label (split('.')[1..-1]), so two unrelated registrations under the same multi-label public suffix compare equal. On an instance hosted at e.g. blog.com.br, a user's website 'http://loja.com.br/products' is classified as same-site and the profile displays the full 'loja.com.br/products' instead of the host alone; because no test in this diff executes this branch at all, the misclassification ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the `elsif` branch triggers when `website_host` and `discourse_host` have the same number of dot labels and that count is > 2, then compares `split('.')[1..-1]` (dropping only the first label). For hosts like `blog.com.br` and `loja.com.br` (both length 3), this compares `com.br` == `com.br` and incorrectly treats them as related, returning `website_host + path` (e.g. `loja.com.br/products`) instead of just `website_host`. The added specs never hit this branch (they cover length 2 vs 2 and 2 vs 3 cases only), so this misclassification would ship untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The equal-host test asserts only the pathed URL ('http://example.com/user'); the diff replaced the context's original bare fixture 'http://example.com' with a pathed one and never pins what website_name returns for a same-domain website with no path, where website_host + URI(website.to_s).path concatenates the empty string. The dominant real-world stored-website shape (bare 'http://example.com') has its display-name result unpinned — a refactor of the concatenation that yields 'example.com/' instead of 'example.com' mangles every same-site profile name while CI stays green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` that concatenates `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` for same-host / parent-host cases, but the new spec fixture was changed to `'http://example.com/user'` and only tests the pathed case. There is no test pinning the behavior for a same-domain website with no path (e.g. `'http://example.com'`), so an implementation tweak that changes how an empty path is represented (e.g. `""` vs `"/"`) could alter `website_name` output without CI catching it. This is a concrete missing edge-case coverage tied to the new serialization behavior, not a proven current defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The else branch detects same-site only in the parent direction (discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)), so 'http://www.example.com/page' on an instance hosted at 'example.com' returns host-only, while the semantically identical sibling case ('www.example.com' on 'forum.example.com') returns the full path. Admins of apex-hosted instances (hostname 'example.com') see the feature silently not apply to their own www-prefixed profile websites; no test pins this asymmetry and nothing in the diff documents it as intended, so it reads as an oversight of the 'same as instance domain' contract in the PR title.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the final `else` only treats the website as “same site” when `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` (i.e., website is a parent domain of the instance). If the instance is apex-hosted (`discourse_host == "example.com"`) and the user enters a www subdomain (`website_host == "www.example.com"`), the method falls through to returning only `website_host` (dropping `URI(...).path`). This asymmetry is directly implied by the diff and is not covered by the added specs (which only test same host and parent-of-instance cases).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The elsif branch matches any two hosts whose labels after the first are identical, so on an instance whose hostname is a registrable domain under a multi-label public suffix (Discourse.current_hostname = 'example.co.uk'), a website on a completely different registrable domain ('http://other.co.uk/some-page') is treated as the instance's own domain and serialized with its full path. Users on .co.uk/.com.au/.org.uk-style instances see the complete URL path rendered as the website name for sites that are not the instance's domain (e.g. 'other.co.uk/some-page' instead of 'other.co.uk'), violating the feature's stated rule (show the full path only when the website domain is the instance domain) and misleading profile viewers; the href stays correct so nothing crashes or links wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the `elsif` branch triggers when both hosts have the same number of dot-labels and that count is > 2, then treats them as “same domain” if everything after the first label matches: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`. For `Discourse.current_hostname = 'example.co.uk'` and `website_host = 'other.co.uk'`, both have 3 labels and the suffix after the first label is `co.uk` for both, so it incorrectly returns `website_host + URI(...).path` (full path) even though the registrable domains differ. This matches the finding and is a real behavior defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The three website_name specs cover only exact-host match, parent-domain match, and different-domain, leaving the elsif subdomain-variant branch (serializer lines 144-146, the 'www.example.com == forum.example.com' case) completely untested. A regression or false positive in the subdomain-matching branch ships undetected by CI; the public-suffix false positive living in exactly that branch ('other.co.uk' vs 'example.co.uk' matching on their shared 'co.uk' tail) is precisely the class of bug these added specs cannot catch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including an `elsif` branch for same-length multi-label hostnames (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forums.example.com`) at lines 144-146. The added specs only exercise: exact host match (`example.com`), parent-domain match (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`), and different-domain (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`). None of the specs set both `website_host` and `Discourse.current_hostname` to 3+ labels with equal length, so the `elsif` subdomain-variant branch is untested, making regressions in that branch harder to catch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] website_name calls URI(website.to_s) up to three times per serialization (lines 138, 143, 146, 149) with the inline `rescue nil` guarding only the first parse, making the method's crash-safety depend on the positional fact that later calls repeat an already-succeeded pure parse; hoisting `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil` plus an early return deletes the redundant parses and the guard asymmetry. Every user-page serialization performs three URI parses, and the next maintainer who extends this method (e.g. adding a .query display) or hoists the parse without carrying the rescue turns any malformed website string — the profile website column is unvalidated free text — into an uncaught URI::InvalidURIError, 500ing every payload that serializes that user.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the diff does call `URI(website.to_s)` multiple times (once for `.host` with `rescue nil`, then again for `.path` in several branches). That redundancy and the uneven placement of the `rescue` are real, diff-grounded maintainability/performance concerns, and hoisting `uri = URI(...) rescue nil` would simplify and avoid repeated parsing. However, as written it does not introduce a crash: the method returns early when `website_host` is nil (including when parsing raised), and the subsequent unguarded `URI(website.to_s).path` calls only execute when the first parse succeeded, so an invalid URI won’t currently 500. The “next maintainer” failure mode is speculative beyond the diff, so this is not a verifiable defect.
